title: 2 Kings Chapter 2 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Kings chapter 2 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Kings Chapter 2 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Kings Chapter 2.

questions.question: From which location did Elijah and Elisha depart when the LORD was about to take Elijah up into heaven?
questions.correctAnswer: Gilgal
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 2:1 states that Elijah went with Elisha from Gilgal when the LORD would take Elijah into heaven.

questions.question: What did Elijah ask Elisha to do when they reached Bethel?
options: Call the sons of the prophets
questions.correctAnswer: Tarry here
questions.explanation: Elijah said unto Elisha, 'Tarry here,' because the LORD had sent him to Bethel (2 Kings 2:2).

questions.question: How did Elisha respond when Elijah told him to tarry at Bethel?
options: He sent a message to the sons of the prophets
questions.correctAnswer: He refused to leave Elijah
questions.explanation: Elisha said, 'As the LORD liveth, and as thy soul liveth, I will not leave thee' (2 Kings 2:2).

questions.question: Who came to Elisha at Bethel and told him about Elijah being taken away?
questions.correctAnswer: Sons of the prophets
questions.explanation: The sons of the prophets at Bethel came forth to Elisha and informed him (2 Kings 2:3).

questions.question: True or False: Elisha was unaware that the LORD would take Elijah away that day.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Elisha acknowledged knowing that Elijah would be taken away, saying, 'Yea, I know it' (2 Kings 2:3).

questions.question: To which city did Elijah tell Elisha to tarry after Bethel?
questions.correctAnswer: Jericho
questions.explanation: Elijah said to Elisha to tarry because the LORD had sent him to Jericho (2 Kings 2:4).

questions.question: Did Elisha agree to leave Elijah at Jericho when asked to tarry?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Elisha again said, 'As the LORD liveth, and as thy soul liveth, I will not leave thee' (2 Kings 2:4).

questions.question: Who came to Elisha at Jericho with the same message about Elijah's departure?
questions.correctAnswer: Sons of the prophets
questions.explanation: The sons of the prophets at Jericho came to Elisha with the message (2 Kings 2:5).

questions.question: What was Elisha's response to the sons of the prophets at Jericho about Elijah's departure?
options: He said, 'Yea, I know it; hold ye your peace.'
questions.correctAnswer: He said, 'Yea, I know it; hold ye your peace.'
questions.explanation: Elisha acknowledged knowing and told them to be silent (2 Kings 2:5).

questions.question: Where did Elijah tell Elisha to tarry after Jericho?
questions.correctAnswer: Jordan
questions.explanation: Elijah said to tarry because the LORD sent him to Jordan (2 Kings 2:6).

questions.question: How many sons of the prophets stood afar off to view by the Jordan?
questions.correctAnswer: Fifty
questions.explanation: Fifty sons of the prophets stood afar off by Jordan (2 Kings 2:7).

questions.question: What did Elijah do with his mantle at the Jordan River?
options: Smote the waters to divide them
Waved it to call the people
questions.correctAnswer: Smote the waters to divide them
questions.explanation: Elijah wrapped his mantle and smote the waters, dividing them so they crossed on dry ground (2 Kings 2:8).

questions.question: What did Elijah offer to do for Elisha before being taken away?
options: Ask what he shall do for him
questions.correctAnswer: Ask what he shall do for him
questions.explanation: Elijah said to ask what he should do before being taken away (2 Kings 2:9).

questions.question: What did Elisha request from Elijah before he was taken away?
options: A double portion of his spirit
questions.correctAnswer: A double portion of his spirit
questions.explanation: Elisha asked for a double portion of Elijah's spirit (2 Kings 2:9).

questions.question: True or False: Elijah said Elisha's request was easy to grant.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Elijah said it was a hard thing to ask but it would be granted if Elisha saw him taken away (2 Kings 2:10).

medium.title: 2 Kings Chapter 2 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Kings Chapter 2 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did Elijah say would happen if Elisha saw him when he was taken away?
options: Elisha would receive a double portion of Elijah's spirit
Elisha would become a prophet immediately
Elijah would leave a written prophecy
questions.correctAnswer: Elisha would receive a double portion of Elijah's spirit
questions.explanation: In 2 Kings 2:10, Elijah explained that if Elisha saw him when he was taken away, Elisha's request for a double portion of Elijah's spirit would be fulfilled. This promise is linked to Elisha's faithful presence in verses 9 and 11.

questions.question: How did Elijah ascend into heaven according to 2 Kings 2?
options: By a chariot of fire and horses of fire
questions.correctAnswer: By a chariot of fire and horses of fire
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 2:11 describes Elijah's ascent into heaven by a chariot of fire and horses of fire, which separated him and Elisha before Elijah was taken up by a whirlwind.

questions.question: What was Elisha's reaction when Elijah was taken up into heaven?
options: He cried out, rent his clothes, and saw Elijah no more
He fell down and prayed silently
He rejoiced and sang a hymn
questions.correctAnswer: He cried out, rent his clothes, and saw Elijah no more
questions.explanation: As stated in 2 Kings 2:12, Elisha cried out 'My father, my father,' referring to Elijah as the chariot of Israel, then he tore his clothes in grief and saw Elijah no more.

questions.question: What did Elisha do with Elijah's mantle after Elijah was taken up?
options: He took it and struck the Jordan River, causing the waters to part
He burned it as a sacrifice
He gave it to the sons of the prophets
He buried it in the ground
questions.correctAnswer: He took it and struck the Jordan River, causing the waters to part
questions.explanation: According to 2 Kings 2:13-14, Elisha picked up Elijah's mantle that had fallen, struck the waters of the Jordan, and the river parted, allowing him to cross on dry ground.

questions.question: What did the sons of the prophets at Jericho recognize about Elisha after Elijah's departure?
options: That the spirit of Elijah rested on Elisha
That Elisha was now the king
That Elisha was a false prophet
That Elisha would leave Jericho soon
questions.correctAnswer: That the spirit of Elijah rested on Elisha
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 2:15 states that the sons of the prophets at Jericho saw Elisha and said the spirit of Elijah rested on him, showing recognition of Elisha’s new prophetic authority.

questions.question: How did Elisha respond when asked to send men to search for Elijah?
options: Initially he refused, but later sent them after being urged
He sent no one and told them to trust God
He sent only ten men to search
questions.correctAnswer: Initially he refused, but later sent them after being urged
questions.explanation: Verses 16 and 17 show Elisha first refusing the request to send men to search for Elijah, then consenting after persistent urging, demonstrating his obedience mixed with discernment.

questions.question: What lesson about obedience can be drawn from Elisha's command 'Ye shall not send' followed by 'Send'?
options: Sometimes persistence in obedience is necessary before action
Elisha was unsure of God's will
Elisha did not care about Elijah's fate
Elisha wanted to test the men's faith
questions.correctAnswer: Sometimes persistence in obedience is necessary before action
questions.explanation: In 2 Kings 2:16-17, Elisha's initial refusal followed by permission after being urged teaches that obedience may involve waiting and reconsideration, reflecting practical discernment in following God's timing.

questions.question: What was the result of the 50 men’s search for Elijah after Elisha sent them?
options: They searched for three days but did not find him
They found Elijah on a mountain
They found Elijah in a valley
They found Elijah by the Jordan River
questions.correctAnswer: They searched for three days but did not find him
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 2:17 records that the men searched for Elijah for three days but did not find him, confirming Elijah’s miraculous departure into heaven.

questions.question: What does Elisha’s statement 'Did I not say unto you, Go not?' teach about trusting prophetic words?
options: It teaches the importance of trusting prophetic instructions fully
It suggests prophets sometimes change their minds
It implies the men disobeyed on purpose
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches the importance of trusting prophetic instructions fully
questions.explanation: In 2 Kings 2:18, Elisha reminds the men that he had told them not to go, teaching that trusting prophetic guidance without hesitation is vital for faithful living.

questions.question: According to 2 Kings 2:10-11, what is the significance of Elisha seeing Elijah taken up?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Elisha’s seeing Elijah taken up was crucial because Elijah said in verse 10 that if Elisha saw him, he would receive a double portion of his spirit, which is fulfilled as Elijah ascends in verse 11.

questions.question: The mantle that Elijah dropped had no significance for Elisha’s prophetic power.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 2:13-14 shows Elisha picking up Elijah’s mantle and using it to part the waters of Jordan, symbolizing the transfer of prophetic authority and power.

questions.question: How does 2 Kings 2:15-18 teach about humility and respect for God’s timing in ministry?
options: Elisha respected God's timing by initially refusing the search and only sending men after being urged
Elisha took pride and immediately sent men to prove his power
The sons of the prophets acted out of impatience and Elisha ignored them
Elisha disregarded the sons of the prophets and acted independently
questions.correctAnswer: Elisha respected God's timing by initially refusing the search and only sending men after being urged
questions.explanation: Verses 15-18 show Elisha’s humility and respect for God’s timing as he first refuses the search for Elijah, demonstrating trust, and only sends men after much urging, highlighting obedience balanced with discernment.

questions.question: In light of 2 Kings 2:10-18, what biblical virtue is demonstrated by Elisha’s persistence in following Elijah and his careful response to the sons of the prophets?
questions.correctAnswer: Faith and discernment
questions.explanation: Elisha’s unwavering presence with Elijah (verse 10), his recognition of prophetic timing, and measured response to requests (verses 16-18) exemplify faith and discernment in ministry.

questions.question: What does 2 Kings 2:18 imply about the consequences of disregarding prophetic counsel?
options: Disregarding counsel may lead to unnecessary hardship or confusion
Disregarding counsel has no real impact
Disregarding counsel always leads to punishment
questions.correctAnswer: Disregarding counsel may lead to unnecessary hardship or confusion
questions.explanation: Elisha’s rebuke in 2 Kings 2:18 after the men returned from searching shows that ignoring prophetic instruction can cause wasted effort and confusion, teaching believers to heed God’s guidance carefully.

questions.question: What does the interaction between Elisha and the searching men teach us about prayerful obedience in challenging situations?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Elisha’s initial refusal and eventual sending of men after persistent urging (2 Kings 2:16-17) highlights the virtue of prayerful obedience and waiting on God’s timing in difficult circumstances.

hard.title: 2 Kings Chapter 2 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Kings Chapter 2.

questions.question: What did the men of the city say about the water and the ground in 2 Kings 2?
options: The water was good, but the ground was barren
The water was naught, and the ground barren
Both the water and ground were plentiful
The water was salty, and the ground was fertile
questions.correctAnswer: The water was naught, and the ground barren
questions.explanation: The men of the city described the water as 'naught' and the ground as 'barren', indicating a problem with the city's resources (2 Kings 2:19).

questions.question: What did Elisha instruct to be brought to him before he healed the waters?
questions.correctAnswer: A new cruse and salt
questions.explanation: Elisha asked for a new cruse (a jar) and salt to put in it before he cast it into the spring to heal the waters (2 Kings 2:20).

questions.question: What was the effect of Elisha casting salt into the waters?
options: The waters became salty and undrinkable
The waters were healed, causing no more death or barrenness
The waters multiplied and flooded the land
questions.correctAnswer: The waters were healed, causing no more death or barrenness
questions.explanation: Elisha declared that the LORD had healed the waters so that from then on there would be no more death or barren land from them (2 Kings 2:21).

questions.question: How long did the healing of the waters last according to the text?
questions.correctAnswer: Unto this day
questions.explanation: The text states that the waters were healed unto this day, indicating a lasting effect (2 Kings 2:22).

questions.question: What did the little children say to Elisha as he was going up to Bethel?
questions.correctAnswer: Go up, thou bald head
questions.explanation: The children mocked Elisha by saying, 'Go up, thou bald head; go up, thou bald head' (2 Kings 2:23).

questions.question: What was Elisha's response to the mocking children?
options: He cursed them in the name of the LORD
He sent them away with a warning
questions.correctAnswer: He cursed them in the name of the LORD
questions.explanation: Elisha turned back, looked at them, and cursed them in the name of the LORD, which resulted in two bears coming out of the woods and mauling 42 children (2 Kings 2:24).

questions.question: Where did Elisha go after the incident with the children?
options: To Mount Carmel and then to Samaria
questions.correctAnswer: To Mount Carmel and then to Samaria
questions.explanation: After the incident, Elisha went to Mount Carmel and then returned to Samaria (2 Kings 2:25).

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently displayed in the passage where Elijah is taken up to heaven?
questions.correctAnswer: Foreshadowing
questions.explanation: The chariot of fire and Elijah's ascension by a whirlwind foreshadow later heavenly ascensions, such as Jesus’ ascension in Acts 1, indicating foreshadowing (2 Kings 2:11).

questions.question: The request of Elisha for a 'double portion' of Elijah's spirit is an example of what kind of Old Testament literary motif?
questions.correctAnswer: Legal inheritance
questions.explanation: Elisha’s request for a 'double portion' reflects the Old Testament legal custom of a double portion of inheritance given to the firstborn son, symbolizing spiritual succession (2 Kings 2:9).

questions.question: What Hebrew word translated as 'mantle' in this chapter symbolizes prophetic authority?
questions.correctAnswer: Mantle (simlāh)
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'simlāh' translated as 'mantle' refers to a cloak or garment symbolizing prophetic authority, as seen when Elijah’s mantle is passed to Elisha (2 Kings 2:8,13).

questions.question: How did the 'sons of the prophets' at Jericho respond after Elisha crossed the Jordan on dry ground?
options: They bowed themselves to the ground before him
questions.correctAnswer: They bowed themselves to the ground before him
questions.explanation: After Elisha crossed the Jordan, the sons of the prophets at Jericho recognized that the spirit of Elijah rested on him and bowed to him in respect (2 Kings 2:15).

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage echoes the miraculous crossing of the Jordan River as seen in 2 Kings 2?
questions.correctAnswer: Exodus 14:21-22
questions.explanation: The parting of the Jordan's waters by Elijah and Elisha echoes the parting of the Red Sea in Exodus 14:21-22, symbolizing God's deliverance.

questions.question: Which New Testament event parallels Elijah's ascension into heaven by a whirlwind?
options: The baptism of Jesus in Matthew 3
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus’ ascension in Acts 1
questions.explanation: Elijah's ascension by a whirlwind foreshadows Jesus’ ascension into heaven as recorded in Acts 1, showing a typological connection (2 Kings 2:11).

questions.question: True or False: Elisha sent fifty men to search for Elijah immediately after Elijah's ascension.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Elisha initially refused to send men but later allowed fifty men to search for Elijah after being urged, showing hesitation rather than immediate action (2 Kings 2:16-17).

questions.question: True or False: The curse pronounced by Elisha on the mocking children resulted in the death of 42 children by two bears.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Elisha cursed the children, and two bears came out of the wood and mauled 42 of them, as stated in 2 Kings 2:24.

theological.title: 2 Kings Chapter 2 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Kings Chapter 2 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Elijah's request for Elisha to 'tarry here' at multiple locations signify about prophetic succession?
options: It emphasizes Elisha's need to remain faithful and witness Elijah's departure
It shows Elijah's desire to abandon Elisha
It indicates that Elisha should go to different cities alone
It reveals Elijah's fear of dying alone
questions.correctAnswer: It emphasizes Elisha's need to remain faithful and witness Elijah's departure
questions.explanation: Elijah commands Elisha to 'tarry here' at Gilgal, Bethel, Jericho, and Jordan (2 Kings 2:1-6), highlighting the importance of Elisha's presence to receive the prophetic mantle and spirit, showing faithfulness in prophetic succession.

questions.question: What theological doctrine is illustrated by Elisha's request for 'a double portion' of Elijah's spirit?
options: The doctrine of spiritual inheritance and empowerment
The doctrine of justification by faith
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of spiritual inheritance and empowerment
questions.explanation: Elisha's request for a double portion of Elijah's spirit (2 Kings 2:9) reveals the biblical doctrine where spiritual authority and power are passed on, empowering successors in God's mission, consistent with inheritance principles (cf. Numbers 27:18-23).

questions.question: How does the miraculous parting of the Jordan River by Elijah and later by Elisha demonstrate God's attribute?
questions.correctAnswer: God's sovereign power over nature
questions.explanation: Both Elijah (2 Kings 2:8) and Elisha (2 Kings 2:14) part the Jordan River, showing God's sovereign control over creation to accomplish His purposes, affirming divine omnipotence as seen also in Psalm 104:3.

questions.question: What redemptive significance does Elijah’s ascent into heaven by a whirlwind have within biblical theology?
options: It prefigures Christ’s ascension and God's victory over death
It symbolizes Elijah's failure to complete his mission
It represents the end of prophecy in Israel
It shows Elijah was taken as a punishment
questions.correctAnswer: It prefigures Christ’s ascension and God's victory over death
questions.explanation: Elijah's heavenly ascent by whirlwind (2 Kings 2:11) typologically foreshadows Christ's ascension, signifying God's triumph over death and the continuation of divine revelation through His chosen servants (cf. Acts 1:9).

questions.question: What doctrinal truth is taught by Elisha's immediate exercise of prophetic power after Elijah's departure?
options: The continuation of God's covenant promises through prophetic succession
The end of divine revelation after Elijah
The rejection of previous prophetic messages
questions.correctAnswer: The continuation of God's covenant promises through prophetic succession
questions.explanation: Elisha taking up Elijah's mantle and performing miracles (2 Kings 2:13-14) illustrates the continuity of God's covenantal work and revelation through successive prophets, affirming God's faithfulness to His promises.

questions.question: How does the response of the sons of the prophets at Jericho to Elisha's new authority reveal a theological principle about communal recognition of God's Spirit?
options: Recognition of the Spirit's resting confirms legitimate prophetic authority
Prophets should work independently without community
Spiritual authority is based on popularity
Miracles are irrelevant to spiritual leadership
questions.correctAnswer: Recognition of the Spirit's resting confirms legitimate prophetic authority
questions.explanation: The sons of the prophets at Jericho acknowledge 'The spirit of Elijah doth rest on Elisha' (2 Kings 2:15), showing that communal recognition of God's Spirit is essential for confirming true prophetic authority and legitimacy.

questions.question: What does Elisha’s refusal to send men to search for Elijah initially teach about trust in God’s providence?
options: It teaches reliance on God's sovereign knowledge rather than human initiative
It shows Elisha's neglect of responsibility
It indicates a lack of faith in God's power
It demonstrates human wisdom over divine will
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches reliance on God's sovereign knowledge rather than human initiative
questions.explanation: Elisha’s initial refusal to send men to search for Elijah (2 Kings 2:16-18) illustrates trust in God’s providential knowledge and timing, emphasizing faith over anxious human efforts.

questions.question: How does Elisha’s healing of the water at Jericho reveal God’s attribute of providence and care for creation?
options: God’s providence actively sustains and restores life
God is indifferent to physical needs
God only cares about spiritual matters
God punishes the land without mercy
questions.correctAnswer: God’s providence actively sustains and restores life
questions.explanation: Elisha’s healing of the water (2 Kings 2:20-21) demonstrates God's providential care and kindness in sustaining creation’s well-being, showing His concern for both spiritual and physical life (cf. Matthew 6:26).

questions.question: What does the judgment on the youths who mocked Elisha reveal about the holiness and justice of God?
options: God’s holiness demands respect and His justice punishes mockery of His prophet
God is indifferent to human disrespect
God’s justice is arbitrary and unfair
questions.correctAnswer: God’s holiness demands respect and His justice punishes mockery of His prophet
questions.explanation: The severe judgment on the mocking youths (2 Kings 2:23-24) reveals God's holiness that requires reverence and His just response to contempt against His anointed servants, affirming divine justice.

questions.question: How does the narrative arc of Elijah’s departure and Elisha’s rise advance the biblical theme of covenant continuity?
options: It shows seamless transmission of God’s prophetic mission across generations
It indicates the end of God’s covenant with Israel
It suggests a break in God’s plan
It highlights human failure to follow God
questions.correctAnswer: It shows seamless transmission of God’s prophetic mission across generations
questions.explanation: The transition from Elijah to Elisha (2 Kings 2:11-14) advances the biblical narrative of covenant continuity, emphasizing God’s unbroken commitment to guide His people through successive prophets.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight do 2 Kings 2:9 and 2 Kings 2:10 provide about the conditions for spiritual blessing and inheritance?
options: Spiritual blessings require faith and perseverance to witness God’s work
Faith is irrelevant to receiving God’s Spirit
questions.correctAnswer: Spiritual blessings require faith and perseverance to witness God’s work
questions.explanation: Elisha’s request for a double portion (2 Kings 2:9) and Elijah’s response emphasizing the necessity to see him taken up (2 Kings 2:10) teach that spiritual inheritance depends on faithful perseverance and witnessing God’s acts.

questions.question: What theological principle is taught by the sons of the prophets’ awareness of Elijah’s impending departure in 2 Kings 2:3 and 2 Kings 2:5?
options: God reveals His plans to His community of prophets
God keeps His plans hidden at all times
Prophets act independently without community awareness
The prophetic office ends with Elijah
questions.correctAnswer: God reveals His plans to His community of prophets
questions.explanation: The sons of the prophets at Bethel and Jericho know of Elijah’s departure (2 Kings 2:3 and 2 Kings 2:5), illustrating that God discloses His purposes to His prophetic community, emphasizing communal revelation.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that the miraculous parting of the Jordan River is legendary and not indicative of divine power. What does 2 Kings 2:8 and 2 Kings 2:14 actually teach about God’s intervention in history?
options: God sovereignly intervenes in nature to fulfill His covenantal promises
Miracles are merely myths without historical basis
God’s power is limited and symbolic
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly intervenes in nature to fulfill His covenantal promises
questions.explanation: The clear narrative of Elijah and Elisha parting the Jordan (2 Kings 2:8, 14) demonstrates God's real and sovereign intervention in natural events to accomplish His redemptive purposes, affirming biblical theism (cf. Exodus 14:21).

questions.question: What combined teaching about divine judgment and holiness emerges when considering 2 Kings 2:23-24 alongside 2 Kings 2:19-22?
options: God’s holiness demands purity and His judgment restores covenant order
God is indifferent to moral conduct
Judgment is arbitrary and unrelated to holiness
questions.correctAnswer: God’s holiness demands purity and His judgment restores covenant order
questions.explanation: The healing of water (2 Kings 2:19-22) and the judgment on mockers (2 Kings 2:23-24) together reveal that God's holiness requires both physical and moral purity, and His judgment serves to restore covenantal order and reverence.

questions.question: How does the presence of the 'fifty men of the sons of the prophets' observing from afar in 2 Kings 2:7 inform our understanding of prophetic community and witness?
options: It shows the importance of communal witness and continuity in God's work
It suggests prophets act in isolation without community
It indicates the prophets doubted Elijah
It means the prophetic office was ending
questions.correctAnswer: It shows the importance of communal witness and continuity in God's work
questions.explanation: The fifty prophets watching from a distance (2 Kings 2:7) emphasize the communal aspect of prophetic ministry, communal validation, and the continuity of God's work through a prophetic community.
